_comment: Complete record of every elevation query made during the 2026-09-05 siting session, including the one that failed. Raw values are exactly as returned by the service - not rounded.

source.units_caveat: The JSON response does not declare units. Meters was requested via the units parameter and the returned magnitudes are consistent with metres AMSL for this location.
source.important_limitation: BARE EARTH. Conifer canopy sits on top of these figures and is NOT modelled. Real horizon obstruction toward any forested bearing will be higher than computed here.

phase_centre_reference.derivation: Feed ground elevation 97.24 m + approximately 9.9 m mean antenna height. Used as the apex of the horizon angle triangle for every radial sample.
phase_centre_reference.note: The final design raises mean height to 12.69 m (phase centre ~109.9 m), which lowers every computed horizon angle by roughly 0.2-0.3 deg. The 107.1 m reference was kept for consistency across the session and is the conservative choice.

site_relief_finding: The build site is flat to within 0.6 m across the entire 33 m run. No terrain correction is needed for the antenna geometry itself.

horizon_by_bearing._comment: Controlling horizon angle per bearing = the maximum obstruction angle over all ranges sampled on that bearing. Positive blocks, negative is open.

250.verdict: OPEN - drops 59 m then recovers; far side sets the horizon at essentially 0

quadrant_summary.NE_0_to_70: Rising hillside. Europe blocked to 5.7 deg, South Africa to 3.4 deg. WORST quadrant.
quadrant_summary.E_SE_90_to_160: Clear to slightly falling. Americas unobstructed.
quadrant_summary.SW_200_to_270: Steep drop-off, -8 deg for 500 m into a ravine. BEST quadrant. Contains NZ (227), Hawaii (240), VK2/3/4 (244-247), VK6 (268).
quadrant_summary.NW_300_to_330: Falling, -4.8 deg at 310. VERY GOOD. Contains Japan (301), China (310), Vladivostok (311), Beijing (318), Alaska (321).

slope_gain_model._comment: How the foreground slope was converted into an effective take-off angle reduction.
slope_gain_model.rule: A downward foreground slope of angle s moves the ground reflection point downhill and far away, effectively raising the antenna many wavelengths above the reflecting plane. Take-off angle is reduced by approximately s.
slope_gain_model.confidence: MODERATE. This is a first-order rule of thumb, not a NEC model. It predicts direction and rough magnitude reliably; treat the exact degrees as indicative.

failed_queries.purpose: LiDAR-derived canopy height at the apex tree, to verify the 35/50 ft support height and find taller trees.
failed_queries.result: HTTP 200 with body {"error":{"code":500,"message":"Error performing identify operation","details":[]}}
alternatives_not_yet_tried: Washington DNR LiDAR Portal at https://lidarportal.dnr.wa.gov/ (bulk download, not a point API)
King County LiDAR DSM via https://kingcounty.gov/en/legacy-en/services/gis/gisdata/metadata/elevation (DSM minus DGM gives canopy height, but distribution is zipped ArcInfo Grid, not a REST query)
NOAA Coast 2016-2017 PSLC Lidar DEM bulk tiles at https://coast.noaa.gov/htdata/raster2/elevation/WA_King_DEM_2016_8589/
failed_queries.workaround_used: Operator confirmed by direct observation that a throw line reaches 50 ft or more in both support trees.
